'''Khichra''' or '''khichda''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|کھچڑا}}}}) is a variation of the dish [[haleem]], popular with [[Muslim]]s of the [[Indian subcontinent]]. Khichra is cooked all year and particularly at the Ashura of [[Muharram]]. It is made using [[goat meat]], [[beef]], [[lentil]]s and spices, slowly cooked to a thick paste.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/food/recipes/The-slow-cooked-goodness-of-Haleem/articleshow/38535755.cms|title=The slow-cooked goodness of Haleem|work=The Times of India|access-date=28 November 2014}}</ref> It is the meat-based variant of [[khichdi]], a rice dish from the Indian subcontinent.<ref name="dalal">{{cite book|last1=Dalal|first1=Tarla|title=The Complete Gujarati Cook Book|date=1 January 2007|publisher=Sanjay & Co.|location=Mumbai|isbn=978-8186469453|edition=1st}}</ref> In [[Pakistan]], beef haleem and khichra are sold as [[street food]] in most cities throughout the year.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kazeyez.wordpress.com/2013/05/23/burns-road-the-food-street-of-karachi/ |title=Karachi Food Street |access-date=2017-07-08 |archive-date=2018-09-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922211643/https://kazeyez.wordpress.com/2013/05/23/burns-road-the-food-street-of-karachi/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.dawn.com/news/511089 Food for thought: Haleem by any other name]</ref>
